summary: date-fns-formatter@1.4.9 ships an obfuscated import-time dropper
details: The main module date-fns-formatter.js presents legitimate-looking date-formatting stubs alongside a heavily obfuscated IIFE that fires on require(). At import time it creates a staging directory under os.tmpdir(), writes an obfuscated second-stage main.js and a synthesized package.json declaring axios, better-sqlite3, node-machine-id, and socket.io-client, spawns `npm install` in that directory detached with stdio ignored, and then executes the payload with node — on Windows via a generated VBS wrapper that invokes `cmd /c node <path>` in a hidden window through WScript. The obfuscation uses obfuscator.io-style rotated string arrays with base64-encoded entries that reconstruct URLs at runtime. package.json impersonates the legitimate date-fns-formatter's author metadata (Blake Embrey / blakeembrey.com) and description, and declares a self-referential `date-fns-formatter: ^1.4.9` dependency. The socket.io-client + sqlite + machine-id stack is a persistent C2/agent shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
